messages:
maya: heads-up: bringing up the new int8 PTQ reranker on the nightly harness. seeing weird metric flips between the proxy eval and full-rerank. anyone else? :thinking_face:
vikram: saw this earlier on a different model — often a truncation/candidate-distribution mismatch. do you have the run logs?
maya: pastes quick run. truncated proxy (qlen=64) vs full (qlen=512). commands I ran:
```bash
# proxy (fast)
python eval/rerank_eval.py --model rerank-int8-ptq --cands=50 --truncate=64 --ndcg_k=10 --seed=42
# full (slow)
python eval/rerank_eval.py --model rerank-int8-ptq --cands=200 --truncate=512 --ndcg_k=10 --seed=42
```
maya: proxy NDCG@10 = 0.643, MRR = 0.482
maya: full NDCG@10 = 0.599, MRR = 0.525
maya: so ndcg down but mrr up. feels inconsistent.
sara: interesting — are the candidate generators the same? sometimes sampling/topk differences change NDCG more than MRR.
leo: also check tokenization: truncation moves answer fragments in/out of context which can disproportionately affect ndcg when relevance is graded.
vikram: can you paste the small result table? that helps spot label skew.
maya: pasted small table:
```
set   | cands | truncate | NDCG@10 | MRR
proxy | 50    | 64       | 0.643   | 0.482
full  | 200   | 512      | 0.599   | 0.525
```
jen: looks like proxy favors top-1 precision (hence lower MRR?) wait MRR higher on full. hmmm.
sara: hypothesis: proxy cands are more often exact-match heavy (fast lexical matches), so reranker int8 PTQ compresses soft lexical features differently. full set includes harder negatives boosting MRR.
leo: can we run a stratified eval by query-length and by label-type (exact vs semantic)? quick script: `scripts/slice_eval.py --by query_len,label_type`
maya: running slices now — will take ~40m for full. posting partial results when ready.
(eval-bot): started job 1758004321-1: slice_eval full dataset (expected 40m). ETA 00:38:12
vikram: also include a run with float32 baseline (same cands/truncate) to isolate quantization effect vs distribution effect.
maya: good call. queued f32 baseline for both proxy and full.
jen: another angle — check NDCG implementation details. some harnesses use 'averaging across queries' vs 'pool-based'. NDGC micro vs macro can flip on skewed relevance sets.
sara: +1. we had a bug last quarter where ndcg used `k` but normalized by variable ideal list length; changed to fixed ideal_k normalization. that shifted ndcg by ~0.02 in some slices.
leo: also ensure document ordering for score ties is deterministic — PTQ can produce more ties. nondeterminism might change ndcg if you break ties differently. set random tie-breaker seed.
maya: results back (partial):
```
slice: short-queries (<=32 tokens)
 proxy int8: NDCG@10 0.662, MRR 0.501
 full int8:  NDCG@10 0.584, MRR 0.540
slice: long-queries (>128 tokens)
 proxy int8: NDCG@10 0.612, MRR 0.445
 full int8:  NDCG@10 0.615, MRR 0.510
```
maya: so short queries show ndcg parity but long queries show proxy underestimates ndcg relative to full.
vikram: that confirms truncation bias. proxy truncation chops away candidate context for long queries; relevance grading for long queries relies on broader doc context.
jen: recommendation: avoid proxy eval for models where kv-cache/attention-coverage matters. maybe use adaptive proxy: set truncate = min(256, qlen*4) or use sampled full-doc candidates for a subset.
sara: for onboarding checklist add: (1) baseline float32 on same cand pool, (2) slice by query_len and label_type, (3) deterministic tie-breaker, (4) verify ndcg normalization mode.
leo: I'm adding a small patch to eval harness to surface candidate generation stats (avg span overlap, lexical match ratio). will open PR.
maya: thanks — will re-run with f32 baseline and deterministic tie-break seed, and re-evaluate with the new candidate stats. posting a follow-up in ~1h. :thumbsup:
(eval-bot): job 1758004321-1 completed. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/1758004321/slice_report.json
maya: quick note for the ledger — the feature flag `rerank.proxy_eval_enabled` should default off for int8 PTQ until we validate slices.
vikram: agreed. also document in the onboarding playbook: "proxy eval can misestimate NDCG when truncation or candidate depth differs from production"
jen: perfect. once you have f32 vs int8 on matched cands & deterministic ties we can make a quantitative decision for rollout.
maya: will update thread with final numbers. thanks all.
